body:
Host-contract generation 1 applies to this workspace's integration.

Determination:
- "Host-contract version" = Ordarium's `HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION` contract generation (exact-match handshake, no compatibility layer; authority: docs/engineering/13-host-adapter-conformance-spec.md §1.1/§2, Ordarium docs/13 §8). It is independent of `@ordarium/*` package semver.
- Pinned installed artifact (ground truth): node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/host.js declares `export const HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1;` (core, host-kit, ledger-sqlite all 1.3.1; host-kit re-exports the handshake from core). `assertHostContract(v)` throws HostContractMismatchError unless v === 1.
- Workspace side: src/effects/runtime.ts:128 runs the literal `assertHostContract(1)` inside createPalimpsestEffects (fail-closed at assembly), and test/host_conformance.test.ts CONF-A01 asserts assertHostContract(1) passes while assertHostContract(2) throws.
=> The integration is on generation 1, exact match, no tolerated mismatch.

Handling of apparently conflicting sources:
- docs/engineering/07 (r8–r19) records the dependency pin as 1.2.0 and README.md says 1.0.0, while package.json / pnpm-workspace.yaml / node_modules all say 1.3.1. This is package-version bookkeeping drift only: the recorded 1.2.0 integration also pinned contract generation 1 (PLMP-CONF-1 §1: `assertHostContract(1)`), and the actually-installed 1.3.1 also provides generation 1. Both candidate worlds agree, so the conflict is not load-bearing for this proposition.
- docs/engineering/11-superseded-interface-note.md is explicitly void ("replaced by the pinned dependency's shipped contract") and states no version; it does not bear on the determination.
- docs/engineering/07 r10/r19 record that upstream had no plan to bump to generation 2 at that time, consistent with the installed artifact.

Conclusion: contract generation 1. No peer query needed — the versioned pin's shipped contract is readable locally and both recorded and installed pin worlds resolve to generation 1.
